_note: Public rules. Each word is a regex, matched as a whole word, ignoring case. In 'lists', order matters: the first list with a match wins. '_doc' is copied into results/0_definitions.md; {name} is filled with that setting's value.

unit._doc: One message that the user typed. The study does not include session summaries, interruption markers, commands, or pastes. A paste has more than {paste_words} words, or it starts with one of these words: {greeting}.

session._doc: A new session starts after a gap of more than {gap_minutes} minutes. Session-level tests do not use sessions with fewer than {min_messages} messages.

domain._doc: The first list with a matching word sets the domain. If no word matches, the message gets the domain of the previous message in the same session. If there is no previous message, the domain is Unclassified. Groups: {groups}.

output_type._doc: The first list with a matching word sets the output type. If no word matches, the message gets the output type of the previous message in the same session. If there is no previous message, the output type is Text.

tone._doc: If both lists match, the tone is Mixed. If one list matches, the tone is the name of that list. If no list matches, the tone is Neutral. A dissatisfied message has one of these tones: {dissatisfied}.

reply._doc: The study pairs each prompt with the next message that the user typed in the same session. A prompt is an included message or a paste, because the agent received the paste. The tone of the next message (Dissatisfied, Satisfied, or Neutral) shows the result of the agent's work on the prompt.

limits._doc: Word lists do not find sarcasm or indirect complaints. Private word lists (names and organizations) stay on the local computer. This file does not show them.
